title: DR Congo's Battery Metals: Cobalt Quotas, Copper and a Price Halved Since April | The Six, Ep. 6
lede: DR Congo mined about 74% of the world's cobalt in 2025 and is now the second-largest copper producer. This episode looks at how Kinshasa is using export bans and quotas to control how much leaves the country, what that did to prices, and who buys.
keyPoints: DR Congo mined an estimated 230,000 tonnes of cobalt in 2025, about 74% of the world's 310,000, and holds half of known reserves (USGS, 2026).
It mined an estimated 3.2 million tonnes of copper in 2025, second only to Chile's 5.3 million (USGS, 2026).

After a cobalt export ban from February to October 2025, quotas cap exports at up to 96,600 tonnes a year in 2026 and 2027, including a 9,600-tonne strategic reserve. An order dated June 29, 2026 bans copper and cobalt concentrate exports.
Cobalt hydroxide rose from $5.90 to $25.25 a pound in 2025 (Benchmark), peaked near $26 in April 2026, and was assessed at $13–14 on Oct. 27 (Fastmarkets).
China produced 79% of the world's refined cobalt in 2025. This week Congo ordered a fraud and smuggling inquiry after seizing more than 500 trucks and thousands of tonnes of copper and cobalt.
